text:
incident-bot: PAGER: hosted-runtime gpupool-4 kvcache memory-pressure -> OOM risk. Prefetch depth and continuous-batcher spike observed. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

devon: Oncall here, joining. Which shard? any customer-facing failures?

alice: gpupool-4, shard s-19. We see sustained prefetch depth jump from 16->128 for some longprompt sessions. Eviction can't keep up.

ben: hitting 5xxs for a small subset of chat customers, ~0.15% overall but trending up. Correlates with long prompt ingestion times.

carol: quick logs: ```
[14:02:33Z] kvcache_prefetch.go:234 prefetch_depth=128 alloc_delta=+24GB
[14:02:34Z] continuous_batcher.go:198 avg_batch=48 -> 512, window_ms=1200 -> 6000
[14:02:35Z] runtime: OOM kill candidate on shard s-19
```

devon: ack. Immediate plan: 1) throttle prefetch depth 2) limit batch window to prevent runaway amplification 3) canary rollback if needed.

alice: proposed temp patch (hotfix): ```
redwoodctl rollout patch runtime/hosted-gpupool-4 
  --set kvcache.max_prefetch_depth=32 
  --set kvcache.prefetch_ttl_ms=2000 
  --set batching.max_tokens_window=2048 
  --canary 5% --canary-duration 10m
```

ben: +1 do canary 5% then 25% if stable. Also add a short term circuit: reject requests with prompt tokens > 200k with 429? customers might see degraded UX but prevents OOM.

carol: added a quick check to the hosted ingress to reject anything with content-length > 1.5MB (effectively limit long prompts). Deployed to ingress-canary.

devon: launching alice's patch now to canary 5%. Watching telemetry dashboards.

incident-bot: Deploy started: rollout id r-2026-739999. Canary 5% -> waiting 10m.

ben: support note: small customer cohort seeing timeouts; sending holding message to affected accounts with ETA 30m. support-lead please coordinate comms.

support-lead: on it, drafting short note: "We observed elevated errors for some requests with extremely long inputs. We're applying temporary throttles; small set of customers may experience rejections for very long prompts. We'll update in 30 minutes."

carol: canary metrics after 5m: memory pressure down 45% on canary nodes, avg batch size back to ~60. 5xx rate on canary nodes down to baseline.

devon: good. bump canary to 25% for 15m. If stable, escalate to full rollout.

alice: patch for permanent fix in review: implement context-length-aware prefetch (cap prefetch proportional to prompt tokens up to hard max 64). Also add more aggressive eviction priority for long-session keys.

ben: customer impact: support reported ~12 customers with transient errors; no major revenue impact. classify as P1- mitigated -> monitoring.

devon: handing off monitoring to ben for next 30m while I continue root cause triage. If any uptick -> page me immediately. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident update logged. Status: mitigation deployed (canary->25%), impact reduced, monitoring. Next update in 30m or on significant change.

carol: will follow up with detailed postmortem draft: root cause looks like combination of an unusual long-prompt campaign + a batching regression that increased batch windows under certain token distributions (amplification loop).

devon: thanks team. Moving to watch mode. Handoff complete.
